title: Part Four, Chapter 12: The Generations of the Kings

verses.t: And these were the generations and the descent of the kingdom, and the glory of Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam, our first grandfathers and fathers, when the sun, the moon and the stars dawned. And here we shall begin the descent of all the kings and lords, as they came in and succeeded one another, as each of the generations of the lords and old lords, of all the clans, died and came in; and here each of the lords of the Quiché will be told of one by one.
Balam-quitzé, the first, and the trunk of the people of Caviquib.
Cocavib, the second generation from Balam-quitzé.
Balam-Conaché, the third generation.
Cotuha-Ztayub, the fourth generation.
Cucumatz-Cotuha, the first of the wonder-workers, the fifth generation.
Tepepul-Ztayul, the sixth generation.
Quicab-Cavizimah, the seventh generation, who was also a wonder-worker.
Tepepul-Ztayul, the eighth generation.
Tecum-Tepepul, the ninth generation.
Vahxaqui-Caam and Quicab, the tenth generation of the kings.
Vucub-Noh and Cuvatepech, the eleventh generation of the kings.
Oxibqueh-Beleheb-quih, the twelfth generation of the kings; and these were reigning when Alvarado came, and they were hanged by the Spaniards.
Tecum-Tepepul, who paid tribute to the Spaniards; and these were the thirteenth generation of the kings.
Don Julio de Rojas and Don Julio Cortés, the fourteenth generation of the kings, and they were the sons of Tecum-Tepepul.

And these are the generations of the kingdom, of the kings of throne and house of the Caviquib-Quichés. And now we shall tell of the chinamits. And these are the great houses of each of the lords and chiefs who were named: nine chinamits of Caviquib, and nine great houses; and this is the name of each of the lords of the great houses:
Ahan-Ahpop, lord of a great house, which was called Cuha.
Ahan-Ahpop-Camha, and his house was called Quiquinaha.
Nimchocoh-Canec, a great house.
Ahan-Atohil, lord of a great house.
Ahan-Cucumatz, lord of a great house.
Popolvinac-Chituy, lord of a great house.
Colmet-Quenay, lord of a great house.
Popolvinac-Pahom-Tzalatz-Xcuxeba, lord of a great house.
Tepeu-Yaqui, lord of a great house.
And these are the nine chinamits of Caviquib, and they had many vassals in their charge.
And here are set down those of Nihaibab, who had nine houses; and first we shall tell the descent of the kingdom, whose trunk was one, before there was light and sun:
Balam-acab, the first grandfather and father.
Coacul-Coacutac, the second generation.
Cochahuh-Cotzibaha, the third generation.
Beleheb-Quih, the fourth generation.
Cotuha, the fifth generation.
Batza, the sixth generation.
Ztayul, the seventh generation of kings.
Cotuha, the eighth generation of the kingdom.
Beleheb-Quih, the ninth generation.
Quema, the tenth generation.
Ahan-Cotuha, the eleventh generation.
Don Cristóbal was the name of the one who reigned in the time of the Spaniards.
Don Pedro de Robles is the one who reigns now.
And these were all the kings who descended from that king Zalel. And now we shall tell the lord of each of the great houses.
Ahan-Zalel, the first lord of the people of Nihaibab, lord of a great house.
Ahan-Ahtzic-vinac, lord of a great house.
Ahan-Zalel-Camha, lord of a great house.
Nima-Camha, lord of a great house.
Vchuch-Camha, lord of a great house.
Nima-Camha, lord of a great house.
Nimchocoh-Nihaibab, lord of a great house.
Ahan-Avilix, lord of a great house.
Ya-Colatam, lord of a great house.
And these are the great houses of the people of Nihaibab, and so the nine chinamits of Nihaibab were called; and each of the lords whose names we told first had many chinamits.
And this is the descent of the people of Ahan-Quiché, from their first grandfather and father:
Mahucutah, the first man.
Cohan, of the second generation.
Cazlacan, of the third generation.
Cocozon, of the fourth generation.
Comahcun, of the fifth generation.
Vucub-ah, of the sixth generation.
Cocamel, of the seventh generation.
Coyabacoh, of the eighth generation.
Vinac-bam, of the ninth generation.
And these were the kings of the people of Ahan-Quiché and their descendants. And these are the names of the lords of the great houses, which are only four:
Ahtzic-Vinac, the name of the first lord of a great house.
Colmet-Ahan, the second lord of a great house.
Nimchocoh, the third lord of a great house.
Hacavitz, the fourth lord of a great house; for there were only four great houses of the people of Ahan-Quiché.

And these were the three great banquet-houses, which were like fathers to all the lords of the Quiché; and the three banquet-houses all met together, and they were the ones that commanded and ordered everything, small and great: the three councils or banquet-houses.
The great council and banquet-house of the people of Caviquib, the second of the people of Nihaibab, and the third of the people of Ahan-Quiché; each of these three in its chinamit.

And this is all there is of the Quiché, for there is no longer anywhere to read it. In ancient times there was, but it has been lost. And here ends all that concerns the Quiché, which is now called Santa Cruz.
